claims.statement: gmmff uses a Redis-backed storage implementation in internal/store/store.go for distributed slot state with TTL-based expiration and atomic operations for slot creation (slot UUID + code mapping).
WebRTC peer connections are established using the Pion WebSocket library (github.com/pion/webrtc/v4) for data channel creation, with DTLS-SRTP encryption handled automatically by the library.

STUN/TURN server configuration for WebRTC NAT traversal uses environment variables GMMFF_STUN and GMMFF_TURN with support for long-term credentials, ephemeral credentials, and server-side ICE push via GMMFF_PUSH_STUN/GMMFF_PUSH_TURN to override client-configured ICE servers.

mDNS (Multicast DNS) enables local network peer discovery in local mode via the internal/localmode/ package implementing DNS-based Service Discovery over Multicast DNS (RFC 6763) for the _gmmff._tcp.local. service type.

Cryptographic libraries including golang.org/x/crypto (for HKDF, HMAC, scrypt) and github.com/decred/dcrd/dcrec/secp256k1/v4 (for elliptic curve operations) underpin PAKE, key derivation for symmetric keys, HMAC-SHA256 for SDP signing, and scrypt for schedule mode password protection.

WebSocket client libraries for browser (WASM) and native clients are implemented in internal/signaging/client_js.go (WebSocket wrapper for WASM) and internal/signaling/client_native.go (using github.com/gorilla/websocket) to connect to the signaling server via WebSocket.

The command-line interface uses the Cobra library (github.com/spf13/cobra) to provide hierarchical commands (create, join, chat, send, local, schedule, serve) with automatic help generation, flag parsing with environment variable binding, and command validation.
WebAssembly/WASM integration provides a browser-based file transfer client built from internal/signaling/client_js.go and served via the HTTP endpoint (/) when the server runs with webclient enabled.

The HTTP/web server in internal/broker/server.go serves landing pages, health checks (/healthz, /readyz), Prometheus metrics (/metrics), configuration (/config.json), and WebSocket upgrades (/ws) with security middleware (CSP, X-Frame-Options, COOP, COEP).

Configuration is managed via environment variables with the GMMFF_ prefix, parsed and validated by functions in internal/broker/uiconfig.go and cmd/gmmff/main.go, supporting byte size, duration, and CIDR list parsing with validation via ValidateEnv() on startup.

Nginx reverse proxy configuration (docs/NGINX.md) provides TLS termination with Let's Encrypt support, WebSocket proxying (proxy_pass with proxy_http_version 1.1), security headers (HSTS, CSP, etc.), rate limiting, and logging/access control for gmmff deployments.

Schedule mode provides encrypted server-side transfers via HTTP API endpoints under /api/schedule/ with AES-256-GCM encryption for data at rest, scrypt-based password protection, and TTL-based expiration, enabled by GMMFF_SHOW_SCHEDULE=true and GMMFF_SCHEDULE_DIR environment variables.

Docker containerization is supported via Dockerfile and docker-compose.yml, exposing port 8080 (WebSocket/HTTP), using .env files for configuration, persisting Redis data via volumes, and providing a healthcheck at /healthz.

Internal abstractions include a storage interface (internal/store/store.go) with Redis and in-memory implementations, privacy-preserving structured logging (internal/log/log.go), and metrics collection via internal/broker/server.go (exposing /metrics endpoint).
